# 0052 — Agent names: a `name` label, generated by clients, grant-safe

**Status:** accepted · 2026-11-16 (owner decisions of 2026-11-15, issue #48)

**Amends:** [0025](0025-core-knows-agents-workflows-own-hierarchy.md) (who can write labels, and inheritance, for the one key `name`). Builds on [0033](0033-satellite-milestone.md) and [0034](0034-agent-communication.md), which already name agents by `<id|name>`.

## Context

Agents are numeric ids. With five `claude` agents in the same repo, nothing in `fleet ls`, the sidebar or a pane header tells them apart. Labels (0025) can carry anything, but nothing sets a name and the GUI shows no labels.

## Decision

### The name is a label

- An agent's name is the label **`name=<value>`**. There is no protocol field and no core change; the core still stores and matches labels without interpreting them.
- A name the user or an agent gives is trimmed and must be 1 to 64 characters, with no control characters, and not all digits (so `fleet <cmd> 42` always means id 42). Clients check this; fleetd only applies 0025's label limits.
- Names are **not unique** in the core. Generated names are unique among live agents (below); a name given by hand may repeat, and lookups by name then report the ambiguity.

### `name` is grant-safe

- Grant and quota selectors (0012, 0019, as label selectors since 0025) **may not select on `name`**. Config that tries is rejected when it is loaded. A name therefore gates nothing.
- Because of that, **the spawner of an agent may set its `name`, including another agent.** This is an exception to 0025's "agents can't write labels" and to "a child may only narrow its parent's labels". A child **never inherits** its parent's `name`; it gets the one its spawner gave, or a generated default.
- The user can always rename any agent. An agent renaming agents (`fleet rename` with a token) is limited to its own descendants like every other token-scoped command (0033, 0034); until the M3 token lands, labels are unauthenticated anyway (0025's M2a note).
- The skill tells agents to pass `--name` when they spawn and still never to set other labels.

### Clients generate the default

- Every spawn gets a name: the one asked for, else a generated default. The core never generates or interprets one, so **clients do**, with one shared function in `fleet-client` (`names::default_name`) that the CLI, the GUI and later spawn paths all call, so they agree.
- **Format:** `<task-word>-<animal>`, lowercase ASCII `[a-z0-9-]`, at most 32 characters, for example `fix the SIGTERM race in fleetd serve` → `sigterm-otter`.
- **Task word** (`names::task_word`): from the agent's prompt, meaning its arguments after the program, ignoring flags (`-x`, `--long`):
  - the words are runs of ASCII letters and digits; stopwords and boilerplate ("you", "working", "issue", "repo", "github", "fix", …), the program's own name, words under 3 characters and bare numbers are skipped;
  - an acronym (written in capitals, like `SIGTERM` or `LTO`) wins, then the longest word, then the earliest; a word is cut to 16 characters;
  - with no such word, an issue reference `#23` gives `i23`;
  - with no prompt, a plain shell (`sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, …) gives `shell`, and any other program gives its cwd's basename (`fleetd`), then the program's name.
- **Animal:** from a built-in list of short animal names, picked by a stable hash (FNV-1a) of the program, args and cwd, so the same spawn gets the same name. It changes only to keep the name unique among live agents: the next animal in the list, and once all are taken, `-2`, `-3`… on the first choice.
- A restart keeps the labels, so the name too (the old agent has ended, so it stays unique).

### Where names show and how they are used

- **CLI:** `fleet spawn --name NAME` (shorthand for `--label name=NAME`; an explicit `--label name=…` counts too), without either the generated default; `fleet rename <id|name> <new>` (a `SetLabels` of `name` only); `fleet ls` has a NAME column, and `--json` already has the labels.
- **Name lookup:** commands that take an agent (`screen`, `history`, `send`, `kill`, `restart`, `rm`, `attach`, `label`, `rename`) take an id or a name. All digits is an id. A name matches live agents first; if no live agent has it, ended ones (so `restart` and `rm` work by name). No match, or more than one, is an error that lists the candidates (`names::resolve`).
- **GUI:** the name is the main text of the sidebar row and the pane header, with `program · id` secondary; other labels are small chips on the row (not `name`, `project`, which the group title shows, or `fleet.*`), each showing `key=value` on hover. The New agent sheet has a Name field prefilled with the generated name, which follows the command as it is typed until the user edits it, and a Labels field (`k=v, k=v`). Rename is a double-click on the name in the row or header, or Rename… in the row and pane menus. New terminal names its shell `shell-<animal>`.
- The sidebar filter (#40), and later the command palette (#29) and the agent switcher (#42), match on names, labels, program, cwd and id through one function (`core::sidebar::query_matches`); the row's shown name is the agent's name.
- This replaces #33's GUI-only display name; #33 keeps the per-agent colour or emoji.

## Consequences

- Agents spawned by old clients, or before this change, have no name; every display falls back to the program (the sidebar) or the OSC title, then the program (the header).
- The heuristic task word is sometimes dull (a long prompt's longest word); `--name` and Rename fix that, and the skill asks agents to pick a short task name.
- When grants and quotas get config (M3 quotas, M7 secrets), their loader must reject a `name` selector, with a test.
